prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places a large desk or tabletop directly in front of the camera wearer across frames 1–4, roughly 0.5–1.5 m away, with the wall and upper room several metres behind it; the monitor/TV areas sit beyond or just above the desk at about 1–2 m. The repeated bright desk edge makes its near-field extent clearer than in RGB, while darker walls and ceiling indicate greater distance, although the nearly uniform regions and abrupt boundaries make metric estimates uncertain. Across frames 1–4, lateral head rotation shifts the same nearby desk and screens from left toward centre and right without clear approach or retreat; parts of the furniture remain cut off below the frame. In frame 5, a person appears close on the right, approximately 0.5–1.5 m from the wearer and within possible arm's reach at the nearer end of that range, facing generally toward the camera; the map separates the person from the more distant hallway, but the bright silhouette lacks reliable internal depth and partly exits the right and lower borders.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently identifies one or two TV/monitor surfaces in frames 1–4, positioned ahead of the wearer and alternating between left, centre, and right as the head turns; one detected tabletop lies immediately below a screen in frame 4. These masks clarify object boundaries and show that the screens are separate objects at similar height and likely within roughly 1–2 m, but segmentation alone does not provide dependable metric distance or front-versus-back ordering. Frame 5 contains a person mask on the far right, partly outside the image, with the head above the torso and the body facing approximately toward the camera wearer; no other person is segmented in the earlier frames. A small region left of the person is labelled "car," but the RGB context does not support that class, and missing masks for much of the desk, walls, and room show that the map is incomplete and unreliable for the full layout.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, so it provides no detected body or hand keypoints, limb directions, interpersonal distances, reach zones, or facing estimates. It therefore adds no spatial structure beyond the RGB and cannot confirm the pose of the person who enters on the right in frame 5. From RGB context alone, that person is close to the camera wearer, partly out of view, and oriented generally toward the wearer, but the absent skeleton prevents reliable claims about gaze, arm position, or whether either person's hands are within reach. The lack of any pose for the visible person indicates detection failure, likely related to partial framing, close range, blur, or low illumination.
